name: Save Khaki United
why: New York chinos, tees and shirts in Supima cotton, sewn in the USA and sold under the Save Khaki United name for about 20 years, with five stores of its own in New York and California.
origin: Founded around 2006 in New York City by David Mullen; the brand marks 20 years in 2026 but states no founding year.

onething.n: Weak evidence: the brand lists SK933 The Original Chino first in its Chino Guide; no page calls it the signature.

price_read.sublines: GOOD WORK (own sub-line, sold under the SKU name on savekhaki.com); SKU California capsule; Port Canvas and Third Party goods excluded

cities: 5 stores across the US, including Los Angeles, New York, Montecito · independent shops, and its own site

craft_evidence.owned: Partial: brand says it built its own sample room in Los Angeles (sample maker Rosendo) - a sample room, not a production plant; no owned factory or mill found
craft_evidence.makers: Yes, in journal and some product copy: Saitex USA (denim wash, LA); Shai-Tex Inc (knitter, Lynwood CA); Cauzza Growers (Supima grower, Buttonwillow CA); CFDCO (key chain); Parkdale Mills (yarn). Not named on most product pages
craft_evidence.mills: Yes on a subset of product pages: Mount Vernon (denim/twill), Inman Mills (Modern Worker Pant), Parkdale Mills (yarn), Candor (poplin). About 9 of 121 styles name a mill or yarn maker; most do not
craft_evidence.madein: 49 of 121 men product descriptions state a made-in line (about 40%); 87 of 121 carry the icon-local-manufacturing tag; 19 tagged imported_textile (Made in USA of imported fabric/yarn). Brand says all SKU-label products are sewn in the USA
craft_evidence.heritage: Dated and placed: "20 Years of Save Khaki United" (2026 article, so about 2006); "born in New York City, not far from our Lafayette shop" (AW26 lookbook). Early chinos were made in China before US production (founder note)
craft_evidence.process: Yes: garment-dyed and finished in California; Supima tee grown, knit, cut, sewn, dyed in USA (spinner closed after 2024 floods, new spinner announced Feb 2026); outerwear passes quilter, cutter, dyer, finisher; Saitex water-saving denim wash; Gerber pattern software
craft_evidence.reasoning: Proposal only. The brand names its knitter, dye house, grower and some mills with specifics, and says every SKU-label garment is sewn in the USA (fabric and yarn sometimes imported, labelled as such). It owns a sample room but no factory or mill found, and most product pages name no maker. That is a 3 (names makers and mills, owns no production) with a case for 3+ on the Supima story; not a 4 until an owned or exclusive production site is shown.

ownership.owner: Not stated by the brand; David Mullen is the founder and creative director.

opview: “Made in USA” isn’t about flag-waving or nationalism. It’s about differentiation. — David Mullen, founder, SKU Behind the Scene (founder note, brand journal, 27 September 2025)
